newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends down, short-dated gilts rise.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends down, short-dated gilts rise.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday easier at 10.25 percent against the day's opening 10.75 percent on lower demand for funds, dealers said.
Dealers said most of the deals on Monday were done around 10.50 percent. "Demand for funds has certainly eased from last week," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Funds also appeared to be available in plenty today."
He said with the reporting Friday coming up on November 23, rates were likely to ease further. "I feel call (money) will be around 10 percent tomorrow and will ease further before Friday."
Dealers said prices of some short-dated securities firmed up on Monday although the market was largely steady in moderate trade.
"With call money seeming to stabilise, there was some interest in short-dated securities," said a dealer. "However the volumes are still quite poor."

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded on Monday at 102.50 rupees against its last traded price of 102.35 while the 13.50 percent 1998 was traded at 102.43 against 102.30 rupees, dealers said.
